latest.title: Understanding AWS IAM: A Beginner's Guide to Cloud Security
latest.description: Learn how AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) helps secure cloud resources by managing users, roles, permissions, and access policies. A beginner-friendly introduction to AWS security fundamentals.

latest.title: Designing an Enterprise-Grade Petrol Pump Management System: Fuel Inventory, Real-Time Sales, Automation, and Financial Reconciliation
latest.description: Explore how to design an enterprise-grade Petrol Pump Management System using Java, Spring Boot, React, PostgreSQL, Apache Kafka, Redis, and AWS. This article covers fuel inventory management, real-time dispenser integration, POS billing, digital payments, shift management, stock reconciliation, fraud detection, financial reporting, and multi-station operations.

latest.title: Designing a Fault-Tolerant Distributed Job Scheduling Platform: Architecture, Execution Guarantees, and Intelligent Workload Management
latest.description: Discover how to design a fault-tolerant distributed job scheduling platform using Java, Spring Boot, PostgreSQL, Apache Kafka, Redis, and AWS. This article explores distributed job execution, scheduling algorithms, worker coordination, transactional outbox, idempotency, retry mechanisms, priority-based processing, workload management, and failure recovery.

latest.title: Day 53: Capstone Backend - Spring Boot Container, ECR and ECS Express Mode
latest.description: Today I containerized the capstone's Spring Boot backend, stored the image in Amazon ECR, and deployed it with ECS Express Mode into yesterday's VPC, connecting it to RDS through a Secrets Manager secret instead of a password baked into the image.

latest.title: Your AI Chatbot Knows a Lot. But Does It Know Your Company's Data?
latest.description: Explore how Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) helps AI applications answer questions using private and frequently updated documents. Learn how to combine Amazon Bedrock, Knowledge Bases for Amazon Bedrock, Amazon S3, AWS Lambda, and API Gateway to build an AI-powered knowledge assistant. This beginner-friendly guide covers RAG architecture, Python implementation, embeddings, document retrieval, security, hallucinations, and production best practices.

latest.title: AWS re:Invent 2026: Being Part of a Global Cloud Experience, Even from Afar 🚀
latest.description: You don't always need to be physically present to be part of something extraordinary. Although I couldn't attend AWS re:Invent 2026 in Las Vegas, I'm excited to join the experience virtually through AWS re:Invent LIVE, learn from industry experts, explore the latest cloud innovations, and connect with the global AWS community.

latest.title: Giving E-Waste a Second Life: How Agentic AI and AWS Could Build Smarter Recycling Systems
latest.description: What if discarded electronics could find a second life? Agentic AI could transform recycling by using specialised agents to identify e-waste, assess reusable components, recommend repairs, and locate recycling centres. AWS services like Amazon Bedrock, Lambda, S3, and DynamoDB could power this system. By combining autonomous decisions with cloud technology, we can build our circular economy where fewer resources are wasted and more materials find a purpose. A smarter, greener future starts here.

latest.title: Graceful scale-in for voice AI agents on Amazon ECS with task scale-in protection
latest.description: A voice AI call can hold an Amazon ECS task for 10 minutes, and new calls keep arriving every few seconds. This post shows how to combine task scale-in protection with application-controlled draining, so a task stops taking calls before Amazon ECS stops the task.

latest.title: Canteen Live: I built a serverless cafeteria tracker for my campus on the AWS Free Tier
latest.description: How I built a free-tier serverless app on AWS (S3, CloudFront, API Gateway, Lambda and DynamoDB) that shows students how crowded the campus cafeteria is, today's menu and dish ratings.

latest.title: Day 07: Writing Production-Ready Dockerfiles: Containerizing a Python Application
latest.description: Containerize a small Flask service twice: a naive Dockerfile, then a fixed one built with multi-stage builds, layer-cache-friendly ordering, a non-root numeric user, and exec-form gunicorn that handles SIGTERM correctly. Includes a no-tools health check and a lab comparing the two images.

trending.title: I Let Claude Code Create My AWS Account
trending.description: No credit card, no access keys, no IAM setup. With agentic account creation, one Claude Code prompt handles sign-up, setup, and deployment.

trending.title: AWS en Nerdearla México 2026: Despliega tu juego mexicano

trending.title: Gemma 4 on AWS Lambda with a GPU: E2B on an NVIDIA L4, Day One
trending.description: AWS Lambda now runs functions on GPU instances through Lambda Managed Instances. Gemma 4 E2B, Google's QAT weights at 4 bits, served by vLLM inside a Lambda function on one g6.2xlarge: how to build it, a local chat page, and what Google's drafter does to speed through Lambda, from 1 to 48 requests at once.

trending.title: Learning the Craft of Technical Speaking: My AWS New Voices Journey
trending.description: A personal reflection on how I changed the way I write a proposal, explain a hard topic, prepare slides and handle a quiet room. I also share how I put these lessons into practice at AWS Community Day Udaipur.

trending.title: 3.4 Million NYC Taxi Trips, Zero Servers: Building an Iceberg Lakehouse on AWS
trending.description: Build a fully serverless data lakehouse on AWS with Amazon S3 Tables, Apache Iceberg, the AWS Glue Data Catalog and Amazon Athena, using 3.4 million real NYC taxi trips. Clean, correct, evolve and time-travel your data with nothing but SQL, for under a dollar.

trending.title: Road to re:Invent 2026: What It Is and How to Watch
trending.description: This year the road is a state of mind: 30 AWS Heroes hack live in see-through cubes at Caesars Forum on Sunday 29 Nov for $100k. Here's how to watch.

trending.title: Teach an agent to fish and it will maintain your code for a lifetime
trending.description: AWS Emulator, a local emulator of AWS services that you can run on your machine to build and test your AWS applications, was written entirely by autonomous AI agents. This article talks about some of the techniques the team employed that taught the agents how to effectively build the AWS Emulator.
